text.p: British composite insurer Guardian Royal Exchange Plc on Wednesday ruled out a share repurchase in the near future while the company looked to grow its businesses by selective acquisitions.
GRE finance director James Morley told Reuters that the industry was experiencing a period of consolidation and opportunity for acquisition probably unrivalled in recent history.
"It doesn't seem to us to make sense to reduce the capacity of the company to make those acquisition at a time the availability of such acquisitions is so great," said Morley.
But he stressed that a sizeable acquisition was not imminent.
"People took what was said at the year-end as meaning there were specific targets in mind -- that was a misreading of the situation."
"We would like to see our life business and in particular the risk transference products of life or health products growing significantly in the UK," he said.
The company also wanted to grow its general business in the UK, Germany, Ireland and the U.S. in selective ways.
That could be done either through organic growth or acquisition if suitable opportunities presented themselves, he said.
"We are on the look out for them but there is nothing of any size imminent," said Morley.
His comments came as the group reported a fall in first half profits as competition and sterling hit results.
Trading profits for the first six months of the year fell to 105 million pounds from 137 million pounds in the same period last year.
While the company was now achieving rate increases in the private motor market sector it had not seen any rapid changes to competitive pressures in other major market sectors.
"Household rates have shown very small increases this year but commercial property remains fairly difficult and there's no sign of reduction of capacity or hardening," said Morley.
In addition to competition and sterling, which reduced trading profits by 9.5 million stg, results were also affected by an increase in subsidence claims to six million sterling.

On a brighter note Guardian Direct and RAC Insurance Direct had 778,000 policies in force at the end of June, an increase of 15 percent on the year-end figure. Average price increase of 10 percent were achieved over the period.
Morley said GRE was very pleased with the progress and said it intended to keep growing the direct writing operation.
"We will grow it at a speed which makes financial sense. Its very easy to stoke the rate of growth by dropping prices but I don't think that the right thing to do," he said.
